summary: PillarHealth: structured-response fragmentation + fallback routing loop causing truncated JSON in production
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 09:42 UTC PillarHealth reported repeated truncated/invalid JSON in structured completions for their clinical-summarization endpoint. Customer observability showed multi-tenant streaming sessions returning well-formed tokens for a few seconds then cutting to partial JSON or closing the stream with HTTP/2 200 but incomplete payload. Impact: 100% of requests for the affected endpoint in us-east-1 were returning unusable structured responses for ~18 minutes; downstream ingestion pipelines rejected outputs causing data loss and urgent remediation requests from the customer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use PillarHealth production API key and call POST /v1/chat/complete with content-type application/json and structured schema enforcement
2) Ensure payload requests redwood-2-medium with stream=true and allow_fallback=true
3) Observe first 0-500 tokens stream correctly, then stream ends abruptly with partial JSON or the server sends final event and closes connection
4) Re-run same request; some runs route to redwood-2-quantized-v1 and show intermittent truncation and duplicate partial completions
comments: 2026-03-10 09:50 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer reports structured JSON payloads truncated mid-object. Collecting request IDs and sample transcripts. Marking P0, paging SRE.

2026-03-10 09:54 UTC - SRE (Ethan): Initial correlation shows high 200-with-body-close events from streaming proxy for sessions routed to quantized pool. Opening router traces and kernel selection logs.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - CS (Marta Lopez): PillarHealth is asking for immediate mitigation and potential invoice credit due to data loss. Customer requests timeline and rollback plan.

2026-03-10 10:12 UTC - SRE (Ethan): Temporary mitigation applied: disabled auto-fallback to quantized variant for PillarHealth routing policy and pinned traffic to redwood-2-medium. Early signs: streaming resumes stable completions.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Support (Aisha): Customer confirms structured outputs are now valid for a subset of requests. Monitoring for recurrence. Preparing incident report and credit calculation.
2026-03-12 16:20 UTC - Engineering (Priya Shah): Root cause analysis committed to PR and scheduled for canary deployment next week. Notifying customer of long-term fix plan.
investigation_notes: Observed pattern: router issued fallback to quantized variant when the serving-runtime reported ~30ms higher initial latency. Fallback triggered mid-request while KV-cache prefix existed, causing incompatible KV cache state between primary and fallback instance.

Streaming proxy (stream-coordinator) emits final 'stream_end' earlier when it receives an unexpected EOF from quantized pool; proxy then signals client close with 200 but no terminal event for structured schema enforcement leading to partial JSON payloads.

Quantized variant used a different tokenization boundary for certain punctuation in clinical text; combined with a stale KV-prefix on the primary, the retransmit/fallback merged two partial generation sequences producing truncated JSON or duplicated fragments.

No signs of hardware OOM or GPU failures. Kernel selection logs show an experimental attention kernel was selected on quantized nodes due to sequence-length heuristics that were recently rolled out in us-east-1 canary the previous night (2026-03-09 02:00 UTC).
Billing exposure: because fallback loop retried and completed partial tokens multiple times, some requests incurred extra token charges. We flagged affected request IDs for billing review.
Relevant traces and IDs: trace_id=trc-20260310-09-47-821, request_samples attached in case file (linked below).
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied 2026-03-10 10:12 UTC: disabled allow_fallback for PillarHealth routing policy and rolled back the attention kernel selection heuristic in us-east-1 canary. Result: stable streaming and full JSON completions resumed.

Customer impact window: 2026-03-10 09:42 UTC - 2026-03-10 10:12 UTC (~30 minutes). We communicated timeline and provided export of failed request IDs to PillarHealth. Customer confirmation of restored service received 2026-03-10 11:00 UTC.

Billing action: flagged affected requests for credit. Finance to compute token-level refund for all request_ids in 'pillarhealth_fallback_exposure_20260310' and issue pro-rated credit. Contact: finance@redwood.com.

Long-term fixes committed: 1) router fallback orchestration to ensure KV-cache compatibility checks before mid-request fallback; 2) streaming proxy to buffer partial sequences and only close stream after terminal event or explicit revert; 3) disable selection of experimental attention kernel until further compatibility tests run across quantized variants. PRs: #3821, #3824.

Post-incident follow-up: schedule cross-team retro with SRE, Serving, Router, and Customer Success. Deliverables: test harness for mid-request fallback, post-deploy synthetic tests for structured schema with stream=true, and customer-facing incident write-up within 72 hours.
Status: Resolved. Engineering patch scheduled for canary 2026-03-17 and full rollout 2026-03-24 pending validation.
